findings.title: Define sequence-slot and digest-head behavior for out-of-order retirement
findings.finding: The envelope does not define its stream key, immutable ownership of each sequence slot, the contiguous head transition, or the previous-digest rule for a noninitial retirement. Later declarations must reference the prior accepted event, declarations with gaps are held, and a valid retirement must apply even with missing earlier declarations. Those rules leave incompatible receiver choices: advancing the head to an out-of-order retirement can skip predecessor integrity/conflict checks; not advancing it leaves later events blocked unless erased/refused predecessor events can be consumed without recreating payload. A new event UUID at an already used sequence slot also lacks an explicit conflict rule.
findings.concrete_case: Receiver has committed declaration 0. It receives authenticated retirement 2 before declaration 1 and must tombstone promptly. Delayed declaration 1 must never recreate covered payload. The draft does not say how the chain commits 1 and 2, or whether unrelated declaration 3 referencing digest(2) can resume. It also does not state whether two different event UUIDs at the same sequence are always a stream conflict.
findings.requested_change: Specify the stream identity and next-contiguous sequence relation; bind each sequence slot and event UUID immutably to exact-byte SHA-256; state all previous-digest rules for both variants. Separate immediate authenticated refusal/tombstoning from ordered chain commitment, and define either safe metadata-only consumption of erased predecessors or an explicit stream-close/recovery policy. Add synthetic conformance for retirement-before-gap, conflicting slot/event, delayed erased predecessor and permitted subsequent stream behavior. Cleanup still uses separately approved authority and cannot revive an old contributor credential.
findings.why_before_implementation: LIB-5A/5B promise an exact contract and deterministic simulator. Their sequence/digest/idempotency behavior cannot be implemented consistently without inventing this protocol rule.

findings.title: Make recipient and cleanup queue bounds concrete before implementing the bounded simulator
findings.finding: The 2,000,000-byte event, 100 admissions/day/human, 20-event batch and five-attempt limits bound individual input and processing, but no aggregate recipient pending-byte/event/stream capacity or cleanup claim limit is specified. Gap-held declarations, disconnected/terminal work and cleanup events that bypass contribution allowance can therefore accumulate indefinitely under the literal acceptance criteria. "Separately enforced aggregate capacity" and "own bounded claims" leave the actual bound and saturation behavior to an unapproved implementation assumption.
findings.concrete_case: A synthetic sender submits sequentially missing declaration events on successive UTC days, or retire events for fresh valid aliases. Batch/retry bounds stay satisfied while the held queue/refusal storage grows. Filling that storage can also prevent the promised tombstone-before-erasure transition unless cleanup reserve and admission behavior are specified.
findings.requested_change: Define bounded, validated configuration/defaults for aggregate retained pending bytes/events and stream count, plus cleanup claims per batch and durable-refusal storage/admission policy. Specify the behavior at capacity, including reservation or safe preflight that prevents declaration admission from blocking durable cleanup, operator attention for exhausted storage, and no eviction of required tombstones. Explicitly label any proposed values/policy unapproved; they need not be claimed measured capacity. Add synthetic saturation tests alongside the existing batch/retry tests.
findings.why_before_implementation: LIB-5B promises queue bounds, priority bounded cleanup and honest acknowledgments. These require an explicit resource/saturation contract rather than only per-event/day/run limits.

private_digest_retention_observation.classification: Held LIB-5C policy choice; no additional blocker for a synthetic-only simulator that obeys payload erasure.
private_digest_retention_observation.assessment: Exact transmitted declaration bytes are private scientific payload and must be erased from drafts/outboxes/receiver stores when covered retirement is acknowledged. The immutable event SHA-256 can support exact-retry conflict refusal without retaining those bytes, but is still derived private integrity metadata with possible linkage/fingerprinting value. It is not a source-file hash or anonymity proof and should not be silently inserted into the minimal tombstone, whose allowed fields exclude such digests.
private_digest_retention_observation.requested_clarity: State that full declaration event bytes do not survive covered erasure, keep event integrity metadata separate from minimal tombstones, and leave any real retained digest/lineage mapping, purpose, retention duration and cleanup authority to an explicit LIB-5C owner/counsel policy. A synthetic LIB-5B acknowledgment proves absence of covered simulator payload only; it cannot certify deletion of remote/unmanaged copies or all derived metadata under a yet-unapproved real policy.
